summary: All three zones resolved to exact records. Ep 138 reopens the ch-229 straddle after the 128-137 filler and runs to ch 231 partial (p.1-10 & 19; ep 139 finishes 231) — continue mid-231. The Forest of Menos graft sits INSIDE ch 247, not between 247/248: ep 146 stops at 247 p.15, eps 147-148 adapt zero manga pages, and ep 149's closing minutes (from ~20:36) adapt 247 p.16-end, so 149 is mixed (type correction) and 146 needs a mid-247 continue point (repair for the page split). Ep 364 promoted to a full record: 468 (p.5-19), 469, 470 (p.1-5 & 17-19), 471, 472 — i.e. ch 470's frame pages already appear in 364 while its Ginjo-backstory bulk is deferred to ep 365's stored out-of-order re-use; continue is the natural 473. Note: bleach.fandom chapter pages carry only a volume/arc-level 'episodes' field (e.g. ch 470 and 472 both say 'Episodes 351-366'), so the per-episode splits rest on the episode pages plus animefillerguide and listfist.

type_corrections.note: Our row types 149 as filler, but it adapts ch 247 p.16-end in its closing minutes (fandom: 'Chapter 247 (from page 16)'; animefillerguide: Mixed, 'only watch from minute 20:36 until the end'). animefillerlist/listfist keep it filler, but the page-level evidence is explicit.

repairs.why: Ep 146 does not adapt all of ch 247 — it stops at p.15; p.16-end is adapted at the end of ep 149 after the Forest of Menos graft. Stored end_chapter 247 stays correct (majority of the chapter), but the record must not imply the chapter is finished (see continue point 247).

flags_for_sean: bleach.fandom chapter pages are NOT a per-episode reverse map: their 'episodes' infobox field is volume/arc-level (chs 229 and 230 both say 'Episodes 126-127, 138-139'; chs 470 and 472 both say 'Episodes 351-366', the whole Lost Agent arc). Per-episode splits for Bleach must come from the episode pages. Also, ch 247's field (eps 144-146, 150-151) skips ep 149 entirely, contradicted by the ep-149 page's explicit 'Chapter 247 (from page 16)' + animefillerguide's minute marks — resolved in favor of the page-level sources.
